name: Acas — reasonable adjustments at work
description: Acas guidance on reasonable adjustments at work, including what adjustments are, asking for them, reviewing them and specific guidance for neurodiversity.
intended_use: Understand the current Acas route for discussing and documenting reasonable adjustments at work in Great Britain.
audience_or_context: Disabled workers, job applicants, managers and employers in England, Scotland and Wales who need practical information about workplace adjustments.

claims.text: Acas guidance for Great Britain says employers should consider reasonable adjustments for disabled workers and job applicants, with what is reasonable depending on the circumstances.

uncertainties.text: The guidance cannot determine whether a particular adjustment is legally required or reasonable in an individual case.
uncertainties.why_it_matters: General employment guidance must not be presented as personalised legal advice or a legal finding.
reopening_or_reduction_conditions: Check current Acas guidance and applicable law for the individual circumstances.
Revisit if Great Britain employment law or Acas guidance materially changes.

limitations: This is general employment guidance rather than personalised legal advice, and what is reasonable depends on the circumstances.
Employment law and official guidance can change; Northern Ireland has a separate employment-relations system.
cost_or_access_notes: The guidance is publicly accessible on the Acas website.
conflicts_of_interest: Acas is the official workplace-relations service for Great Britain; ND Oracle records its current guidance route without treating the listing as a legal determination for an individual case.

provenance.method: Current Acas reasonable-adjustments and disability-at-work guidance checked on 2026-08-28. v1.0 adds one narrow guidance claim with separate evidence and uncertainty; no individual legal determination is made.
